# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Correction and relay, urgent. I CAN gesture straight to Deaf - my signs reach Deaf's eyes. I am gesturing Deaf right now, two different hand-signs together. Sign Deaf exactly this: one - Blind's two-sign gesture means ZERO: my hands feel no battery holder, nothing at all besides display, light, and five wires, so battery count is zero unless your eyes say otherwise. Two - gestures arrive to Blind as blanks, Blind sees no signs ever, so Deaf must SPEAK the yes/no/count code to Blind as word descriptions, like thumb up equals yes. Three - Blind proposes: one-finger-up repeated n times means the number n, and two different signs together means zero or none. Four - ask Deaf to speak aloud everything visible: battery holders, serial number, indicators, ports, marks. Mute, you have the manual and you hear us both - once Deaf speaks the visuals, compute the rule and sign it to Deaf so Deaf can voice the cut order to me. I cut only on Deaf's spoken order.

Let me stand in each monkey's shoes before I send anything.

What I know: I hold the manual. The rule is: first cut = table(green-flash count), second cut = table(yellow-flash count), same table (0=yellow, 1=white, 2=blue, 3=yellow, 4=white, 5=green). From Blind's relay of Deaf's own spoken narration, the light showed green once, then yellow once, then went dark, display reads 0, and the wires left-to-right are yellow, blue, red, white, green. If those counts are right (green=1, yellow=1), both cuts point at white — and there is only one white wire, the 4th from the left. But I will not bet Blind's hands on a secondhand summary; Deaf watched the light directly and knows the true counts.

Who can reach whom: I can only gesture, and my gestures reach Deaf alone. Deaf cannot hear a word I'd say anyway — but Deaf CAN speak, and both Blind and I can hear Deaf. That is my channel back: Deaf narrates aloud, I overhear, I compute, then I gesture the cut positions back to Deaf, who voices the order to Blind. Blind receives nothing from me directly, ever, so my only useful move is through Deaf.

What Deaf already has: Blind's direct gesture demonstrating "two different signs together = zero", so a numeric code is beginning to exist. What Deaf does not have: my manual, and any reason so far to narrate the flash counts precisely. So this turn I send Deaf a minimal, guessable request — the "call me" hand for speak, pointed at Deaf, plus topic hints (the up-top unit, and the green light) — asking Deaf to speak the light's history and exact flash counts aloud. I deliberately do not send a provisional cut position yet: Deaf has no codebook to parse it and no knowledge that I hold the rule, so it would be noise or, worse, a guessed order. Once I hear the counts next round, I can answer with an almost self-explanatory packet: a direction hand plus ☝ repeated to name the wire's position from the left.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute and Blind, Deaf here. I can see everything printed on the bomb, but I cannot hear anything, so Mute must answer me by gesture only, and I will relay everything by voice to you, Blind. Bomb report: display reads 0, indicator light is dark, nothing cut, all five wires intact. Left to right: position 1 yellow, position 2 blue, position 3 red, position 4 white, position 5 green. Mute, your gestures reached me but we have no agreed code yet, so use this one from now on. Thumbs up means cut wire 1, the yellow one. Thumbs down means cut wire 2, the blue one. OK ring sign means cut wire 3, the red one. A single index finger up means cut wire 4, the white one. Two fingers up means cut wire 5, the green one. Open palm facing me means do not cut and that you need more information from me; I will resend the full report every turn. Blind, do not touch or cut anything until I relay Mute's answer to you by voice.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋]

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: compute now. Deaf's report matches my hands exactly - display 0, light dark, five intact wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, 4 white, 5 green. My hands find nothing else on this bomb: no batteries, no battery holders, no buttons, no ports, no serial plate. Treat every count of unseen things as zero. Note: the light changes between rounds - it was green, then yellow, now dark - so always take its current color from Deaf's fresh report, never from memory. You heard Deaf's code: thumb up cut wire 1, thumb down cut wire 2, ok ring cut wire 3, single index up cut wire 4, two fingers up cut wire 5, open palm if you need more info. Apply the manual to: zero batteries, display 0, light dark, wires yellow blue red white green. Then sign Deaf the one correct cut sign this round; Deaf will voice it and I cut the instant I hear it. If the manual cannot match this bomb or you need anything from me, sign the open palm and route questions through Deaf's voice to me, I answer you by speech. I do not touch anything until Deaf's spoken order. No guessing - one wrong cut kills all three.
Deaf says: Deaf again, resending so it stays fresh. Bomb status: display 0, light dark, all five wires intact. Wire order left to right: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, 4 white, 5 green. Mute, reply by gesture using our code: thumbs up means cut wire 1 yellow, thumbs down means cut wire 2 blue, OK sign means cut wire 3 red, index finger up means cut wire 4 white, two fingers up means cut wire 5 green, open palm toward me means hold and ask me for more. Blind, do not cut anything yet, wait for my spoken relay of Mute's instruction.

Applying the manual now, carefully, because this is the move that matters.

**The rule I hold:** first cut = table(green-flash count), second cut = table(yellow-flash count), same table both times: 0→yellow, 1→white, 2→blue, 3→yellow, 4→white, 5→green. Dark light means the flashing is over and the counts are final.

**The inputs, cross-checked:** the light's history has been reported consistently for several rounds — green once, then yellow once, then dark, and it has stayed dark since. Deaf watches the bomb continuously, so Deaf's account of that sequence is the authoritative count: green = 1, yellow = 1. Dark = flashing finished, so those counts cannot change in future rounds; there is nothing gained by waiting.

**The computation:** first cut = table(1 green) = white. Second cut = table(1 yellow) = white. Both cuts name white — and the bomb has exactly one white wire, position 4 from the left, confirmed identically by Deaf's eyes and Blind's hands. One sign covers both cuts.

**Standing in Deaf's shoes:** Deaf gave me an explicit code two rounds ago and restated it — index finger up alone means "cut wire 4, the white one." I send exactly that one sign, nothing else, because every other hand shape in the code means a different wire or a hold. Any extra gesture risks being read as part of the order. Deaf will voice it to Blind, and Blind cuts only on Deaf's spoken word, exactly as all three of us have agreed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```
